title: judge next route is workspace blind over HTTP
summary: For the SWE-Bench-CL adapter: GET /judge/next (both eager ?node= and the global cursor queue) reads state.overlay / state.workspace HARDCODED in routes/judge.js — it ignores the workspace query param. So an isolated per-sequence eval workspace CANNOT read its autowired candidate edge set or pending-dup clusters over HTTP. POST /judge/verdict IS workspace-targetable (targetOverlay). Bridge: the adapter drives the judge WITHOUT reading the queue, using the {note_key, match.key} the POST /overlay/note response returns on a dup-guard fire — it posts a markDistinct verdict (clears pending_dup so the provisional note becomes recall-visible) plus a keepEdge for the autowired note to its match. Two gotchas: (1) markDistinct/markJudged are NOT in the /judge/verdict bare-body fallback allowlist (routes/judge.js line ~132) — they MUST be wrapped as {verdicts:[{markDistinct:...}]} or applied is a silent no-op; (2) the dup guard fires at cosine>=0.70, so consecutive similar CL experiences land pending_dup invisible until judged — a flat force:true store hid this entirely.
